Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap is the sweet spot for Kenshi on Deck, delivering smooth motion while keeping thermals manageable; FSR at a mild render resolution recovers visual quality lost from the lower render target. Drop Shadow Distance to Low if frame rate dips in busy towns.

profiles.Summary: Kenshi is a demanding open-world sandbox RPG that runs on an older engine but is CPU-heavy due to its large simulated world and squad AI, often bottlenecking even modern hardware; it achieves a Platinum rating on ProtonDB and runs well through Proton with no major compatibility issues. Expect 25–40 fps depending on area complexity and squad size, with busy towns and large battles being the most taxing scenarios on the Steam Deck.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from Kenshi's PC minimum/recommended requirements, its known CPU-heavy simulation workload, and the Deck's Zen 2 / RDNA 2 hardware capabilities — monitor frame rate carefully in large towns on first run and adjust TDP or settings accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Kenshi's main bottleneck is the CPU, so lowering GPU load via reduced resolution and FSR upscaling frees thermal headroom for the CPU to handle AI simulation. Avoid large town centres to maintain the frame cap in this profile.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz / 40 fps lock pairs well with the OLED panel and keeps pacing smooth; expect drops into the low 30s in the most populated areas, which is acceptable at this cap.
